Starting with no network: the device is asked for wireless debugging over and over until it stays on. This can take up to two minutes before it starts or gives up.
A USB start uses the classic ADB port, and reopening it needs a network. Connect to Wi-Fi once, or use the wireless start above.
USB start uses the ADB port, which needs a network connection to open again. Since Start without Wi-Fi is on, Shizuku will use wireless debugging instead.

Please start pairing by performing the following steps:
- Navigate to "Developer Options"
- Enable "USB debugging" and "Wireless debugging"
- Tap the left side of "Wireless debugging"
- Tap "Pair device with pairing code"
- Input the pairing code in the notification

On Android 14, installing/updating Shizuku with the Package Installer revokes the ^1 permission, which is required to enable the accessibility service for pairing.

To grant it, run the following ADB command:

^2

After running the command, you may continue with the pairing process.

Note: you can bypass this by installing/updating Shizuku with ADB.

Automatic pairing reads the code out of the system dialog through Shizuku's accessibility service, so it has to be enabled. Shizuku normally enables it on its own, and that needs the WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS permission, which a fresh install has not been granted yet.

Enable it on the next screen, type the code yourself under Manual, or grant the permission once:

adb shell pm grant moe.shizuku.privileged.api android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS

The service turns itself off once the code is found, or after a minute to save power.

Please start pairing by performing the following steps:
- Navigate to "Developer Options"
- Enable "USB debugging" and "Wireless debugging"
- Tap the left side of "Wireless debugging"
- Tap "Pair device with pairing code." Shizuku will automatically detect the pairing code.
The system requires the pairing dialog to always be visible. Using split-screen mode is the only way to let this app and the system dialog be visible at the same time.

Pair without typing a code:

1. Developer options → Wireless debugging
2. Pair device with pairing code

Shizuku reads the code and port straight from that dialog and starts itself. Keep the dialog open until pairing finishes.
A notification from Shizuku will help you complete the pairing.
Navigate to \"Developer Options\", then enable \"USB debugging\" and \"Wireless debugging\".
Tap the left side of \"Wireless debugging\", then tap \"Pair device with pairing code.\" Enter the code in the notification to complete pairing.
The pairing process needs you to interact with a notification from Shizuku. Please allow Shizuku to post notifications.
MIUI users may need to switch notification style to \"Android\" from \"Notification\" - \"Notification shade\" in system settings.
Otherwise, you may not able to enter the pairing code from the notification.
Go back to Shizuku and start Shizuku.
Shizuku needs to access the local network. It is controlled by the network permission.

Some systems (such as MIUI) disallow apps to access the network when they are not visible, even if the app uses a foreground service. Please disable battery optimization features for Shizuku on such systems.
If you are using Magisk, you can try %1$s. For root users, it will eventually replace Shizuku. Note, existing applications need to change a little to use %2$s.

Shizuku cannot switch wireless debugging on without the WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS permission. Turn it on yourself under Developer options > Wireless debugging, or grant the permission with adb shell pm grant moe.shizuku.privileged.api android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS. Once Shizuku is running it keeps that permission itself, so this is a one-off.

The ADB connection closed while starting. Try again.

No local ADB port is open Android clears it on every reboot, and reopening it needs a connection to borrow. Connect to Wi-Fi and Shizuku will reopen it over wireless debugging, run adb tcpip 5555 from a computer, or turn on Start without Wi-Fi to start over wireless debugging instead.
Root is no longer available on this device, so Shizuku can\'t start over root. Pick another start method.
The system start method must be started from the app.

This device does not ship the component the system start uses (com.sdet.fotaagent), so there is nothing to escalate with here. Switch the system start method to Custom command: the app will show you what to run with an escalation your device does have.

The service did not appear within a minute. Both halves keep a log: the starter under ShizukuServiceStarter and the hand-over under BinderSender. A logcat reader filtered to those two shows whether the starter got as far as forking the server, and whether the server ever asked for the binder.
Escalate however you can, your own exploit, an automation or a root shell, and run this command: it launches the service as the system uid. The app is waiting for it to appear.
